A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoDial work. Their main text, algorithms, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite additions and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original STAR and MultiWOZ experiments, model comparisons, ablations and prompt-optimization results, including Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark experiments and adds a human study, Qwen results, code-generation reliability measurements and cost analysis.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes the stated intent-detection input from conversation history to the current utterance and adds slot variables to the fallback LLM input. Expanded helper-update steps largely explain behavior already documented in Appendix A.2 and the retained code examples. The CHIEF/GCG/CHF architecture remains unchanged.

E1.justification: STAR, STARv2 and MultiWOZ dialogue coverage is retained. Section 5.3 adds a limited human assessment task involving three graduate students judging responses and interpretability. The Qwen configuration and additional domain breakdowns do not introduce new dialogue datasets or domains.

E2.justification: Existing benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged. SAM is additionally used in the human comparison, while MARS and SOLOIST join the single-versus-multi-domain JGA analysis in Table 11. These methods already appeared in the overall benchmark comparisons.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a distinct human evaluation protocol using 50 sampled turns, preference judgments, understanding ratings and repair-confidence ratings. It also adds syntax-validity testing across STAR schemas, per-task cost accounting and evaluation with Qwen3-30B-A3B Instruct. Existing benchmark metrics and oracle settings are retained; newly stated dataset counts do not establish changed sampling.

E4.justification: New analyses examine human-perceived interpretability, confidence in repairing responses, code-generation success and syntax failures, task-dependent resource costs, and baseline performance across domain settings. These substantially broaden the diagnostic evidence beyond v2's retained RI, DST/NAP, oracle-state and prompt-optimization ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions report benchmark means over three runs. v3 additionally reports ± values for human understanding ratings, without identifying the dispersion statistic, and a one-tailed paired t-test with p < 0.001. Table 8 newly specifies four code generations per schema, totaling 96; this does not establish increased runs for existing benchmarks.

E6.justification: Existing Table 1 and Tables 3–5 scores are retained. New results include Qwen's 55.1 F1, 57.4 accuracy and 23.04 BLEU; understanding ratings of 4.27 versus SAM's 2.46; 86% syntax success; and $1.63 per 1,000 dialogues. Table 11 adds domain-specific baseline results, but its MARS/SOLOIST multi-domain values of 35.9/35.5 are not reconciled with Table 1's 35.5/35.9.

T1.justification: The conversation/state definitions, Equations 1–3 and Appendix Algorithms 2–3 are retained. No new theorem, proof, assumption or derivation appears. Algorithm 1's additional set notation explains helper bookkeeping rather than introducing substantive new mathematics.

C1.justification: v3 adds the human study as an explicit contribution and shifts the abstract's application emphasis from expert guidance in high-stakes domains to human guidance in unseen domains. Its abstract also replaces the STAR-SOTA/MultiWOZ-parity distinction with broader benchmark-SOTA wording, although the introduction and conclusion retain the original distinction.

C2.justification: v3 adds a NAP–DST synergy interpretation and a cost-versus-annotation rationale. Limitations expand possible domain-transition mechanisms and their pitfalls, while removing the statement that interpretability is demonstrated only indirectly. User accessibility remains unresolved, and Appendix A.7 interprets self-reported repair confidence as evidence of modifiability.

D1.justification: v3 adds the exact Qwen variant, participant recruitment and instructions, and token/cost breakdowns. Conversely, v2's explicit SacreBLEU and regex template-matching details and model-access date window are removed. Code/data access statements and the modified NeMo implementation information remain.

R1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds dialogue-schema induction work by Sreedhar, Lu and Hattami and positions it as complementary to CoDial. It also discusses Guidance, LMQL and RAIL alternatives and explains choosing Colang. New guardrail-survey and Qwen citations extend the background without changing the central positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract and introductory passages are edited, Algorithm 1 is expanded, and dataset/baseline explanations move into the main text. New Colang background and human-study sections are integrated into the existing narrative. Most methodological and experimental prose and the overall section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: New Tables 6, 8, 10 and 11 display human ratings, generation reliability, costs and domain comparisons; new Figures 8–9 show study instructions and per-task costs. Table 1 is regrouped, and the execution diagram moves from appendix Figure 4 to main-text Figure 2. Existing code and schema illustrations are retained.

improvement.justification: The human study and reliability/cost analyses add useful direct evidence for interpretability and practical operation that v2 lacked. The gains are limited by three technically trained participants and reliance on ratings and repair confidence rather than demonstrated corrections. Unreconciled baseline JGA assignments in Table 11 and removed evaluation details are small drawbacks; the core benchmark evidence remains intact.
